title: Checkout resolution is copied from `validate frontmatter`
description: `resolveTemplatePath` repeats the project lookup in `validateFrontmatterAction` (validate.ts:154-166): `resolveProjectWorktree`, `store.getById`, the "Project not found" and "No projectPath configured" UserErrors, then `resolveOperationPath`. Other commands (build, plan, task, slice, arch, check, prompt) carry the same block too. The copy is not identical: validate.ts adds `?? project.projectPath`, which is redundant because `resolveOperationPath` already falls back to `projectPath` (worktree-overlay.ts:24). CLAUDE.md prohibits duplicated logic. Extract one helper in `utils/project.ts` and call it from both validate commands.

title: `'slice-design'` is defined a second time
description: `SLICE_DESIGN_DOC_TYPE = 'slice-design'` duplicates a value that already exists as the schema key and docType value in `FRONTMATTER_SCHEMAS` (frontmatterSchema.ts:74-76) and in `FILENAME_SEGMENT_TO_DOCTYPE` (frontmatterSchema.ts:148). CLAUDE.md requires a value used in comparisons to be defined once. Export one constant from `frontmatterSchema.ts`, reference it there, and import it here.

title: The usage error bypasses the CLI error contract
description: The no-files check throws `SliceDesignValidationError`. The same file uses `UserError` for its other two failures, and `ErrorCode` already defines `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for this case (utils/errors.ts:5; used at project.ts:416). Effects: in human mode the message gets an `Error:` prefix (errors.ts:66) instead of the clean UserError form, and in JSON mode `code` is `UNKNOWN` instead of `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Use `new UserError('no files given. Usage: cf validate design <file...>', 'INVALID_ARGUMENT')`.

title: A swallowed read error is reported as a doctype failure (exit 1), not exit 2
description: `validateFile` calls `parseFrontmatter(file)` at line 95 and never checks `frontmatter.found`. That parser has a blanket catch that converts *any* read failure into `{ found: false, data: {} }` (`packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/frontmatterParser.ts:63-64`). So if a file disappears, changes permissions, or errors on read after `preflight` (`:72-86`) succeeded, the early return at `:96-98` emits `{ pass: false, missing: [], reason: 'doctype' }` instead of an error. The CLI then prints `FAIL <file>` plus the frontmatter message and exits 1 — exactly the "partial results alongside an error" and wrong-exit-code case the file header (`:1-8`) and slice 214's success criteria say must be exit 2 with empty stdout. The `readFile` catch at `:102-105` cannot help: it is unreachable on this path. The same file is also read twice (`:95`, `:102`), which widens that race; a legitimate no-frontmatter document also returns `found: false`, so checking `found` alone cannot separate it from an I/O failure. Read the file once with explicit error handling and parse frontmatter from that text, then add a fault-injection regression test for a read failure after preflight (the existing `sliceDesignFiles.test.ts` only covers failures caught by preflight).

title: `--json` error mode is derived from raw argv, so the command's `-j` alias emits plain-text errors
description: `withJsonOption` (`packages/cli/src/options.ts`) registers `-j, --json`, but `handleError` at `:104` decides its output format from a module-level flag (`packages/cli/src/utils/errors.ts:32-38,47`) that is set only by `packages/cli/src/index.ts:178` via `process.argv.includes('--json')`. `cf validate design -j missing.md` therefore produces JSON results on stdout for successful runs but a human `Error: ...` line on stderr for exit-2 failures, contradicting the structured-error contract in `docs/AGENT-INTEGRATION.md:16` that makes this command a machine gate. `CF_JSON=1` hides the problem, which is why it only shows up for flag-driven use. There are now two sources of truth for "is this a JSON invocation" (parsed `opts.json` vs. global argv sniffing); derive the error mode from the parsed option (or detect `-j` as well) so the alias behaves identically.

title: The machine-readable failure path is never asserted by the new command tests
description: The `run()` helper (`:127-131`) registers `registerValidateCommand` on a bare `Command` and never imports `packages/cli/src/index.ts`, so `setJsonMode()` is never called and `handleError` always takes its plain-text branch in this suite. The six `--json` exit-2 cases (`:205-211`) assert only `cf exited 2`, empty stdout and empty `console.log`; no test asserts that stderr carries `{ "error": true, ... }`, and the one error-message assertion (`:216-222`) runs without `--json`. Consequently neither the documented JSON error payload nor the post-preflight I/O failure mode from the first finding has any regression coverage, even though `--json` is the primary agent/CI interface for this command. Add a case that enables JSON error mode (as the real entrypoint does) and pins the stderr payload for `--json` and `-j` failures, plus a case that fails a read after preflight.

title: The `slice-design` docType literal is now scattered across four places instead of one
description: The change introduces `SLICE_DESIGN_DOC_TYPE = 'slice-design'` as a canonical constant, but the same literal is still hardcoded in the pre-existing frontmatter registry: `packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterSchema.ts:76` (`values: ['slice-design']`), `packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterSchema.ts:148` (`slice: 'slice-design'`), and `packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterSchema.ts:185` (`docType === 'slice-design'`). AGENTS.md is explicit: "Never scatter comparison values across code. If a value is used in conditionals, switch cases, or lookups, define it once … Changing a value should require editing exactly one place." As written, renaming the docType requires editing four files, and the new constant is dead weight because nothing else consumes it. Either have `frontmatterSchema.ts` import `SLICE_DESIGN_DOC_TYPE` (or move the constant into a shared, browser-safe module both can import without a cycle), or drop the new constant and reuse the registry's existing spelling — but do not leave both spellings live.

title: Project resolution and the "Project not found" message are duplicated across two command files
description: `resolveTemplatePath` in `packages/cli/src/commands/validateDesign.ts:34-46` repeats the project-resolution preamble that already exists in `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts:160-172`: constructing a `FileProjectStore`, calling `resolveProjectWorktree({ project: opts.project }, store)`, calling `store.getById(id)`, and throwing the byte-identical user-facing string `Project not found: '${id}'. Run cf project list to see available projects.` The only real difference between the two is the final step (one checks `project.projectPath`, the other checks the resolved checkout root). AGENTS.md requires "Do not duplicate logic. Respect DRY" and defines shared values once. Extracting a single helper into `packages/cli/src/utils/project.ts` — e.g. `resolveProjectCheckout(opts)` returning `{ project, checkoutRoot }` and owning the not-found error — would remove the duplicated message and keep the two `validate` subcommands from drifting as resolution rules evolve.

title: Valid YAML comments cause false docType failures
description:
Valid frontmatter such as `docType: slice-design # design document` is rejected. The reused `parseFrontmatter` retains the inline comment in the value, so this comparison reports a missing docType even when correctly declared.

Use YAML-aware parsing that handles comments without corrupting quoted values, and add regression tests for commented plain and quoted docType declarations.

title: Frontmatter read errors are swallowed, so the later read-error handling is unreachable
description:
`validateFile` calls `parseFrontmatter(file)`. I read that function: it never throws, and any read error returns `{ found: false, data: {} }`. If a file becomes unreadable or disappears after `preflight`, the user gets a `docType` failure ("frontmatter must declare 'docType: slice-design'"). That message points at the wrong cause. The explicit `readFile` try/catch a few lines later, which throws `cannot read file`, can then only fire if the read fails after the first read succeeded.

The file is also read twice, once in `parseFrontmatter` and once in `readFile`. Reading it once and parsing the frontmatter from that text, or reading first and then calling the parser, would give one read and consistent errors.

title: Tests assert against living project docs and a guide-managed template
description:
`PASSING_DESIGNS` hard-codes four real slice documents under `project-documents/user/slices/` (212, 213, 214 and 928). Both new test files copy or read `project-documents/ai-project-guide/.../slice-design.md`. That guide directory is managed by `cf guides update`.

- **Slice docs:** an ordinary edit to one of these slice docs, such as renaming a heading, would fail the CLI suite even though the validator is correct.
- **Template:** a template change published to the guide would do the same. It could also change the expected `missing: ['## Value']` output, or the `## Overview` and `### Verification Walkthrough` assertions in `packages/core/tests/schema/sliceDesignFiles.test.ts:44-50`.
- **Missing checkout:** the tests also fail if the guide isn't checked out, for example in a tarball-style install.

The project rule that fixtures must contain the real production format is a good reason to keep one real-world case. The rest should use a small committed fixture, for example `tests/fixtures/`, for both the template and the designs. That would let the broken-heading and docType cases be built from a frozen design instead of regex-editing 214 (`/^## Value\n[\s\S]*?(?=^## Technical Scope$)/m`). This regex also depends on 214's section order. A single "passes the real template and a real design" smoke test can stay.

title: Project and worktree resolution is duplicated from `validate frontmatter`
description:
`resolveTemplatePath` repeats the sequence in `validate.ts:154-166`:

1. construct `FileProjectStore`
2. call `resolveProjectWorktree`
3. call `getById`
4. throw the same "Project not found" `UserError`
5. check `projectPath`
6. call `resolveOperationPath`

The "Project not found" message string is also duplicated. The project's DRY rule applies here. Extract a shared helper, for example `resolveCheckoutRoot(opts)` in `utils/`, and use it from both commands. The new code also differs from `validate.ts` in one way. It throws when `resolveOperationPath` returns nothing, where the frontmatter command falls back to `project.projectPath`. Failing explicitly matches the "no silent fallback" rule, but a shared helper would settle which behaviour is intended.
